cards.text: Right before this, God's people heard words of comfort, and a picture of God carrying His lambs close to His heart like a shepherd (Isaiah 40:1, 11). Now Isaiah, the prophet (Isaiah 1:1), starts asking BIG questions. The first one: “Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, or marked off the heavens with the span of his hand?”

cards.question: The prophet keeps going: who has weighed the mountains on a scale and the hills with a balance? With these questions, who is the prophet pointing to?

cards.text: Then the prophet asks, “Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or informed Him as His counselor?” Give God advice? Friend, I need a sticky note just to find my own rolling pin.

cards.question: The prophet says God once needed someone to teach Him the paths of justice and the way of understanding.
Now the prophet turns to the nations. How does he say the nations look next to God?

answers.text: Like a drop in a bucket

cards.text: Then the prophet points to Lebanon, a land known for its cedar trees (1 Kings 5:6). Picture all its trees as fuel and all its animals as one burnt offering.

cards.question: All of Lebanon's wood and animals together would be enough for a burnt offering to God.

cards.text: Then the prophet sums it up: “All the nations are as nothing before Him; He regards them as nothingness and emptiness.”
Then the prophet asks it straight: “To whom will you liken God? To what image will you compare Him?” Go ahead, friend, name something.
He brings up an idol. A craftsman casts it, and a metalworker covers it in gold and fits it with silver chains.

cards.question: Then there's the one lacking such an offering. What does he choose for his idol?
The man making a wooden idol also looks for a skilled craftsman to set up the idol so it will not topple.

cards.text: An idol you have to keep from tipping over? Friend, I stand on a gold base too, so PLEASE don't pray to me. Then the prophet asks, “Do you not know? Have you not heard?”

cards.question: The prophet says where God really sits. Where is He enthroned?

answers.text: Above the circle of the earth

cards.question: From where God sits, the earth's dwellers are like ___.

cards.text: As for the sky, “He stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in.” Friend, it takes me three hops and a prayer just to hang up my apron.

Then the prophet says, “He brings the princes to nothing and makes the rulers of the earth meaningless.” And then a picture from the field: “No sooner are they planted, no sooner are they sown, no sooner have their stems taken root in the ground…”

cards.question: When God blows on the rulers, they ___.

cards.text: Remember the question about who God compares to? Now the Holy One asks it Himself: “To whom will you liken Me, or who is My equal?”
Then the call goes out: “Lift up your eyes on high: Who created all these?” Look up, friend, at the stars.

cards.question: The prophet says God leads out the starry host by number. What does He do for each star?

answers.text: He calls each one by name
He gives each one a season
He hides each one by day

cards.question: Because of God's great power and mighty strength, not one of the stars is missing.

cards.text: Now the prophet speaks to God's people as Jacob and Israel, after their forefather Jacob, whom God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28). And they've got a complaint.

cards.question: What are Jacob and Israel saying about the LORD?

answers.text: Their way is hidden from Him
He is angry with them forever

cards.text: The prophet comes right back: “Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth.”

cards.question: The prophet says the everlasting God will grow tired and weary.
What does the prophet say about the LORD's understanding?

answers.text: No one can search it out
Only the priests can learn it

cards.question: The LORD gives power to the ___ and increases the strength of the weak.

cards.text: Then the prophet says, “Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall.” Even young men stumble? Then I feel a LOT better about tripping over my own mustache.

cards.question: Even youths grow tired and weary. But who does the prophet say will renew their strength?

answers.text: Those who wait upon the LORD
Those who bring gifts to the LORD
Those who fast before the LORD

cards.text: Then the prophet says they “will mount up with wings like eagles…” Friend, the highest I've ever flown is a hop onto the cooling rack.

cards.question: Those who wait upon the LORD will run and not grow weary, and they will walk and not faint.
